items.text: In adults with incidental imaging findings that carry a follow-up recommendation, how do tracking approaches (report codes, tracking lists, navigators, clinician alerts, letters to patients and their combinations) compare in reported follow-up completion, where does the loop break, and which patients are missed?
items.population: Adults with incidental imaging findings that carry a follow-up recommendation
items.intervention: Tracking approaches: report codes, tracking lists, navigators, clinician alerts, letters or portal messages to patients, and combinations
items.comparator: Free-text recommendations without tracking, or another approach
items.outcome: Follow-up completion within the recommended interval, with its window and denominator; failure points; results for patients without a primary care clinician and emergency-only patients

finer: Feasible in three months with two radiologists and three librarian days; interesting to the committee and to clinicians; novel as a comparison across approaches; ethical as a literature review; relevant because it decides a budget choice in January 2027.
summary: One review question with completion, failure points and equity as the three strands.
